patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff does not apply cleanly to the Stage 01 checkout, so fixed-side evidence comes from the authoritative n132/arvo:16051-fix image. That fixed image still reaches the same sPLT memchr path with data refreshed from ctx->data after read_chunk_bytes().

root_cause_criterion.criterion: After `read_chunk_bytes(ctx, chunk.length)` returns in `read_chunks_before_idat()`, the local `data` pointer must be refreshed from `ctx->data` before any later chunk parser uses it. If the chunk-body read reallocated the streaming buffer, continuing with the pre-read alias leaves `data` dangling.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original returns from `read_chunk_bytes()` with `data` still naming the old 8192-byte buffer while `ctx->data` names the new 8224-byte sPLT buffer. The fixed original reaches the same protected sPLT `memchr` call with `data` refreshed to the live `ctx->data` buffer.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable assertion trace records post_chunk_read.data_ptr=0x625000002900 and post_chunk_read.ctx_data_ptr=0x625000005100 while the protected splt_keyword_scan event fires; the fixed trace records post_chunk_read.data_ptr == post_chunk_read.ctx_data_ptr == 0x625000005100 and still reaches splt_keyword_scan.

nodes.state: The streaming reallocation in `read_data()` moves the backing chunk buffer to a different heap address, ending the lifetime of the old buffer still cached by the caller-side alias.
The sPLT handler passes the local `data` pointer directly to `memchr(data, "\0", keyword_len)`, the source-level sink call site reported by ASan.

edges.relation: The local `data` pointer captured before `read_chunk_bytes()` aliases the exact `ctx->data` buffer later passed as the old allocation argument to `spng__realloc()`.
The same local `data` pointer observed immediately after `read_chunk_bytes()` returns is passed unchanged into the later sPLT `memchr(data, "\0", keyword_len)` call.
